Convert an XLSForm to a Word or PDF document

Source: R/convertxlsform.R
convertxlsform.Rd

Reads an XLSForm (as used by Open Data Kit and KoboToolbox) and writes a formatted paper version for interviewing and review. The default output is a Word document next to the input file. A PDF is made by converting the Word document with LibreOffice (or Microsoft Word through the doconv package); see docx_to_pdf() and has_libreoffice().

Usage

convertxlsform(xlsform, output = NULL, format = NULL, lang = NULL, ...)

Arguments

xlsform

Path to an XLSForm (.xlsx, .xlsm or .xls).

output

Output file or folder, see Details. NULL (default) writes next to xlsform.

format

"docx", "pdf", "both" or c("docx", "pdf"). NULL (default) takes the format from the extension of output, and is "docx" when there is no such extension.

lang

Language to use: a code ("fr"), a name ("French") or the full header suffix ("French (fr)"). NULL (default) uses the default_language of the settings sheet, or the first language found. See xlsform_languages().

...

Further options, all named. Defaults are in brackets.

  • nested_serial_numbers (TRUE): number questions inside groups as 1.1, 1.2; FALSE gives flat numbers 1, 2, 3.

  • include_relevants (TRUE): show skip logic ("Ask if: ...").

  • include_constraints (TRUE): show constraints.

  • include_hints (TRUE): show hints and guidance hints.

  • include_choice_name (TRUE): show the choice code after each choice label.

  • show_variable_names (FALSE): show the variable name of each question.

  • include_hidden (FALSE): include hidden types such as calculate, start and end.

  • media_root (folder of xlsform): where images, audio, video and external choice files are looked up.

  • title (NULL): form title; overrides form_title of the settings sheet.

  • page_size ("A4"): "A4" or "letter".

  • orientation ("portrait"): "portrait" or "landscape".

  • margins_in (1): page margins in inches, above 0 and at most 2.

  • font_family ("Arial"): font for the document.

  • font_size (11): base font size in points, 6 to 20.

  • template (NULL): a reference .docx whose styles are used.

  • max_choices (30): choice lists longer than this get a code box layout instead of a printed list.

  • strings (NULL): named list overriding connective phrases such as "Ask if".

  • repeat_copies (1): number of blank copies printed for each repeat group, 1 to 20.

  • font_family_cs (NULL): font for complex scripts; chosen from the language when NULL, using the first installed font of a list for the script (for Bengali: Noto Sans Bengali, then fonts that ship with macOS and Windows).

  • lang2 (NULL): a second language, printed on a new line under each label, hint and choice of the first. See xlsform_languages().

  • include_skips (TRUE): print "Go to" instructions next to the choices of single-choice questions whose answer skips later questions.

  • rtl (NULL): lay the document out right to left. NULL decides from the script of the first language (Arabic and Hebrew are right to left).

  • repeat_layout ("auto"): how repeat groups are drawn. "roster" draws a table with one row per member and one column per question (up to 10 simple questions); "copies" prints the questions repeat_copies times; "auto" uses a roster for repeats of up to 6 simple questions and copies otherwise.

  • roster_rows (5): number of rows in a roster when the repeat count is not a fixed number (1 to 50).

  • overwrite (FALSE): replace existing output files.

  • verbose (TRUE): print progress messages.

Value

The path or paths of the files written, as a character vector, invisibly.

Layout

A group with the table-list appearance whose questions share one choice list (up to 8 choices) is drawn as a grid, one row per question. So is a run of questions with the list-nolabel appearance after a question with the label appearance, which gives the column headings and takes no number.

Fonts in PDF output

When the form uses Bengali, Arabic, Devanagari, Ethiopic or Hebrew text, the files of the chosen complex-script font are handed to LibreOffice for the conversion, so the PDF uses the font even when LibreOffice does not find it on its own. A warning names the font when it is not installed. More font files can be given with options(convertxlsform.fonts = ...), see docx_to_pdf().

Where the file goes

  • output = NULL: same folder and base name as xlsform, with the new extension.

  • output is an existing folder: <base name>.<ext> inside it.

  • output is a file path: used as given. Its extension (.docx or .pdf) sets format when format is NULL, and must agree with format otherwise.

  • Two formats (format = c("docx", "pdf")) write two files with the same base name. With a file path in output, its extension is replaced.

An existing file is never replaced unless overwrite = TRUE.

See also

xlsform_outline() to inspect a form before converting it, docx_to_pdf(), and cli() for the terminal.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "minimal", "minimal.xlsx",
                    package = "convertxlsform")
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "minimal.docx")
convertxlsform(path, output = out, verbose = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)

# \donttest{
# A multilingual form: another language, flat question numbers, US letter
path_ml <- system.file("extdata", "multilang", "multilang.xlsx",
                       package = "convertxlsform")
convertxlsform(path_ml, output = tempdir(), lang = "bn",
               nested_serial_numbers = FALSE, page_size = "letter",
               verbose = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)

# PDF needs LibreOffice
if (interactive() && has_libreoffice()) {
  convertxlsform(path, output = tempdir(), format = "pdf",
                 verbose = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)
}
# }
